To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

mobile phones are being transformed from communication tools to networked personal measurement instruments, and that these personal instruments enable an entirely novel genre of mobile computing called citizen science, which can be applied to the domain of environmental awareness.
mobile phones can be used as personal instruments that enable citizens to become active stakeholders by collecting, sharing, and remixing measurements of their city.
“The use of mobile phones as personal instruments for citizen science enables people to become active participants, stakeholders, and agents of change in their community.”.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the potential of the mobile phone as an instrument for citizen science, and the impact of this novel form of urban informatics.
the role of mobile computing in enabling new forms of urban citizen science that are empowering, community driven, and that enable the public to take an active part in the shaping of their cities.
the design of new urban informatics tools to enable citizens to become active participants in the urban environment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

this work is an important step towards empowering individuals to take ownership of their city, and to become active participants in the design, construction, and maintenance of their urban environments.
citizen science is a new genre of urban informatics that is enabled by mobile phones and the Internet.
the mobile phone has evolved from an instrument that connects people to an instrument that connects the city.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are designing a new kind of urban computing system that empowers people to become active stakeholders in their environment.

we are designing and implementing a novel system that empowers citizens to become active participants in the urban environment by enabling them to collect, share, remix, and act on their environmental data.

we are exploring how to empower people to become active stakeholders in their own urban environment by providing them with the means to measure their environment and to share their measurements in a way that enables collective community participation.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the new “networked mobile instruments” enable an important shift in mobile computing usage – from communication and information tool to personal measurement tool that empowers individuals to become active stakeholders and change agents.

mobile personal measurement devices enable a new genre of mobile computing called citizen science that can be used to enable individuals to participate in the creation of the urban environment they live in.
by enabling citizens to measure their city, they are empowered to become active stakeholders and participants in their community, thus enabling a more sustainable urban future.
